p:0.h: Iran's ambassador to Russia says Tehran is ready for 'normal' talks

p:1.h: Dubai International Airport suspends operations after interception nearby

p:4.h: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon kill eight, Lebanese health ministry says

p:6.h: Two bombings targeting police in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa kill at least four

p:7.h: Nightclub bombing in Trujillo, Peru, injures at least 33

p:9.h: Kuwait Petroleum Corporation cuts crude output and refining as a precaution

p:11.h: Sudan launches hepatitis B vaccination campaign for newborns

p:13.h: Trump says U.S. formally recognizes Delcy Rodríguez's government in Venezuela

p:14.h: Child murderer Ian Huntley dies after being attacked by a fellow inmate

p:15.h: Explosive device detonated at protest outside NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani's residence

p:17.h: Guinea dissolves 40 political parties, including the main opposition groups

strategic_conclusion: March 7 showed both escalation and first signs of hesitation in the Iran war: President Trump threatened broader strikes while Iran's president apologized to Gulf neighbours and said attacks on them would pause, even as rockets targeted the U.S. embassy in Baghdad and Dubai's airport halted operations. Energy-policy responses in Washington, Brussels and Kuwait reflected the war's economic reach. Beyond the Middle East, Russia's barrage on Kharkiv, deadly floods in Nairobi, the RSP's lead in Nepal's election, the U.S.-led Shield of the Americas launch and Guinea's dissolution of opposition parties were the day's other major developments.
